Self-supervised learning (SSL) addresses the label scarcity, and cross-modal SSL further exploits the complementarity between co-...

IV. EXPERIMENTALEVALUATION
To evaluateCroCoMAE, we design an experimental study
covering two SAR-optical RS benchmarks, for scene classifi-
cation and semantic segmentation. We compare against both
standard uni-modal SSL methods and recent cross-modal ap-
proaches. We conduct an ablation study where the contribution
of each component ofCroCoMAEis assessed, explore the
interplay between CLS and patch tokens, and analyse the be-
haviour ofCroCoMAEvarying the size of the shared subspace.
Finally, we provide a visual inspection of the segmentation
maps produced byCroCoMAEand representative competing
approaches and a discussion on computational costs.
Datasets.We evaluateCroCoMAEon two downstream tasks.
In both cases, Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2

Experimental Settings.All SSL approaches share the same
data, backbone and fine-tuning setup, and are pre-trained with
AdamW [32] (weight decay 0.05) for 260,000 steps (batch
size 512), with a maximum learning rate of1.5×10 −4, a
linear warm-up of 20 epochs, followed by cosine annealing
with warm restarts. We evaluate single-modal (SAR, Opt) and
multi-modal (MM) settings, the latter obtained by concatenat-
ing per-modality embeddings before the classification head.
Fine-tuning uses two labeled regimes (1% / 10% of data, with
the remaining 99% / 90% held out for testing) under two
strategies: Linear Probing (LP, frozen encoder) and Full Fine-
Tuning (Full-FT, all weights updated), for 300 epochs with
batch size 64. ForDFC2020, LP denotes a frozen encoder
with a trainable segmentation head.

Fine-tuning uses two labeled regimes (1% / 10% of data, with
the remaining 99% / 90% held out for testing) under two
strategies: Linear Probing (LP, frozen encoder) and Full Fine-
Tuning (Full-FT, all weights updated), for 300 epochs with
batch size 64. ForDFC2020, LP denotes a frozen encoder
with a trainable segmentation head.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains align well with empirical results in Tables II, III, and IV, demonstrating notable benefits especially in dense prediction tasks (semantic segmentation) and lower-label linear probe settings. Subspace similarity and CKA analyses confirm that the shared component captures common cross-modal features while the unshared component maintains distinct information.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is tested across two standard remote sensing benchmarks (EuroSAT-SAR for scene classification and DFC2020 for semantic segmentation) under linear probing and full fine-tuning with 1% and 10% label regimes. Baselines include both uni-modal and cross-modal SSL methods (e.g., DeCUR, CROMA) retrained under a strictly controlled shared backbone and training budget, supported by comprehensive ablation studies.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Downstream performance was evaluated on benchmark ground-truth test labels on EuroSAT-SAR and DFC2020, as well as representation similarity checks via CKA and cosine similarity.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard downstream task metrics (weighted F1 score and mean IoU) computed against ground-truth human annotations on held-out test splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Unsupervised pretraining losses consisting of patch-level MAE reconstruction, shared-subspace patch InfoNCE contrast, and CLS intra-modal InfoNCE contrast, followed by task-specific cross-entropy supervision during fine-tuning.

primary.limitations: The pre-training requires separate forward passes for augmented and masked images, leading to higher GPU compute time compared to single-pass designs like CROMA. The evaluation is focused on Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical data without validation yet on other modality pairs.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed with explicit token routing, objective definitions (InfoNCE for CLS and shared patch alignment, MSE for masked patch reconstruction), and architecture choices based on ViT-Small. The design avoids learnable routing parameters by splitting patch token embedding dimensions directly into shared and unshared components.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a clear and conceptually well-motivated contribution to cross-modal representation learning in remote sensing, backed by rigorous experimental controls and baselines evaluated across multiple runs with reporting of variance. The empirical evaluation and ablations solidly substantiate the claims.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces CroCoMAE, a cross-modal self-supervised learning framework for SAR-optical remote sensing that combines within-modality image-level contrastive learning on the class token, patch-level masked autoencoding reconstruction, and patch-level cross-modal contrastive alignment constrained to a shared subspace while leaving an unshared subspace unconstrained.
